sentences.zh: 顯德五年春正月癸未朔，帝在楚州城下，從臣詣行宮稱賀。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the fifth year of Xiande, on guimou the first day of the month, the Emperor was below Chuzhou city; his attendants went to the traveling palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifth year of Xiande, on the first day of the first month (guimou), the Emperor was at the foot of Chuzhou; his followers went to the mobile palace to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·馬仁瑀傳》：世宗征淮南，登楚州水寨飛樓，距城百步，城卒詬罵，左右射莫能及。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Ma Renyu in the Longping Collection: When the Emperor Shizong campaigned in Huainan, he ascended the flying tower of the Chuzhou water fort, one hundred paces from the city; the city soldiers reviled and cursed him, and those beside him shot arrows but could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Ma Renyu in the Longping Collection: When Emperor Shizong campaigned in Huainan, he climbed the flying tower of the Chuzhou water fort, a hundred paces from the city wall. The garrison soldiers hurled abuse, and the men beside him shot arrows but could not reach them.

sentences.zh: 召仁瑀至，應弦而斃。）〉

translations.literal: Renyu was summoned forth; at the twang of the bowstring he fell dead.)]
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renyu was called forward and dropped dead the moment the bowstring sounded.)]

sentences.zh: 乙酉，降同州為郡。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Tongzhou was reduced to a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Tongzhou was demoted to commandery status.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛將軍王環卒。

translations.literal: Wang Huan, General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, general of the Right Xiaowei Guard, died.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，右龍武將軍王漢璋奏，攻海州。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Wang Hanzhang, General of the Right Longwu Guard, memorialized that he was attacking Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Wang Hanzhang of the Right Longwu Guard reported that he was attacking Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔：「諸道幕職州縣官，並以三周年為考限，閏月不在其內，州府不得差攝官替正官」云。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict stated: "Officials in staff posts and prefectural and county offices in all circuits shall alike take three full years as the term for performance review; intercalary months are not counted within this, and prefectures and districts may not dispatch acting officials to replace regular officials," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an edict declared that staff and prefectural and county officials in every circuit would be reviewed on a three-year term, intercalary months excluded, and that prefectures must not send acting officers to replace regular ones.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤權知揚州軍府事。

translations.literal: On jichou, Han Lingkun, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Cavalry, was ordered to serve provisionally as administrator of the Yangzhou military government.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Han Lingkun, commander-in-chief of the palace cavalry, was ordered to act as provisional administrator of the Yangzhou military government.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，發楚州管內丁壯，開鸛河以通運路。

translations.literal: On gengyin, able-bodied men within Chuzhou's jurisdiction were mobilized to open the Guan River so as to clear a transport route.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the authorities drafted able-bodied men from Chuzhou's jurisdiction to open the Guan River and establish a supply route.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝親攻楚州。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Emperor personally attacked Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Emperor personally assaulted Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時今上在楚州城北，晝夜不解甲胄，親冒矢石，麾兵以登城。

translations.literal: At that time the Present Emperor was north of Chuzhou city; day and night he did not remove his armor, personally braved arrows and stones, and directed the troops in scaling the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Present Emperor was north of Chuzhou; day and night he kept his armor on, exposed himself to arrows and stones, and led the troops up onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 丙午，拔之，斬偽守將張彥卿等，六軍大掠，城內軍民死者萬餘人，廬舍焚之殆盡。

translations.literal: On bingwu, it was taken; the false defending general Zhang Yanqing and others were beheaded; the six armies plundered on a great scale; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians within the city died; dwellings were burned almost entirely away.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the city fell. The rebel defender Zhang Yanqing and others were executed. The six armies looted heavily; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians inside the city perished, and nearly every dwelling was burned to the ground.

sentences.zh: （陸遊《南唐書·張彥卿傳》云：保大末，周世宗南侵，彥卿為楚州防禦使。

translations.literal: (Lu You's Biography of Zhang Yanqing in the History of Southern Tang states: At the end of the Baoda era, Zhou's Emperor Shizong invaded south; Yanqing was defense commissioner of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (In Lu You's Biography of Zhang Yanqing in the History of Southern Tang: At the end of the Baoda reign, Emperor Shizong of Zhou marched south, and Yanqing was defense commissioner of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 周師銳甚，旬日間，海、泰州、靜海軍皆破，元宗亦命焚東都宮寺民廬，徙其民渡江。

translations.literal: The Zhou army was very sharp; within ten days Haizhou, Taizhou, and the Jinghai Army were all taken; Yuanzong also ordered the palaces, temples, and common dwellings of the eastern capital burned and the people moved across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou forces pressed hard. Within ten days Haizhou, Taizhou, and the Jinghai garrison all fell. Yuanzong ordered the palaces, temples, and civilian houses of the eastern capital burned and the population moved south across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 世宗親禦旗鼓攻楚州，自城以外皆已下，發州民浚老鸛河，遣齊雲戰艦數百，自淮入江，勢如震霆烈焰。

translations.literal: Shizong personally directed banners and drums in the attack on Chuzhou; everything outside the city had already fallen; he mobilized the prefecture's people to dredge the Old Guan River and sent several hundred Qiyun warships from the Huai into the Yangtze, their momentum like thunderbolts and blazing flame.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong himself directed the assault on Chuzhou with drum and banner. Everything beyond the walls was already in Zhou hands. He drafted prefectural laborers to dredge the Old Guan River and sent several hundred Qiyun warships from the Huai into the Yangtze with the force of thunder and fire.

sentences.zh: 彥卿獨不為動。

translations.literal: Yanqing alone was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing alone did not waver.

sentences.zh: 及梯沖臨城，鑿城為窟室，實薪而焚之，城皆摧圯，遂陷。

translations.literal: When scaling ladders and battering rams reached the wall, they bored into the wall to make chambers, filled them with firewood and burned them, the wall was all shattered and collapsed, and thus it fell.
translations.idiomatic: When siege ladders and rams reached the walls, the attackers tunneled chambers into the masonry, packed them with fuel, and set them ablaze until the fortifications crumbled and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 彥卿猶結陣城內，誓死奮擊，謂之巷鬥。

translations.literal: Yanqing still formed battle lines within the city, vowing to die and fighting fiercely; this was called street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing still drew up ranks inside the city, swore to fight to the death, and battled street by street.

sentences.zh: 日暮，轉至州廨，長短兵皆盡，彥卿猶取繩床搏戰，及兵馬都監鄭昭業等千餘人皆死之，無一人生降者。

translations.literal: At dusk the fighting shifted to the prefectural offices; long and short weapons were all exhausted; Yanqing still seized a rope bed to fight; when Military Supervisor Zheng Zhaoye and more than a thousand others had all died, not one man surrendered alive.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk the fighting had moved to the prefectural compound. Long and short weapons were spent, yet Yanqing seized a rope bed and kept fighting. Zheng Zhaoye, military supervisor, and more than a thousand others died; not one man surrendered alive.

sentences.zh: 周兵死傷亦甚眾，世宗怒，盡屠城中居民，焚其室廬，然得彥卿子光祐不殺也。

translations.literal: Zhou soldiers also suffered very many dead and wounded; Shizong was enraged and slaughtered all residents within the city and burned their dwellings, yet when he captured Yanqing's son Guangyou he did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou casualties were also very heavy. Shizong in his anger massacred the city's inhabitants and burned their homes, yet he spared Yanqing's son Guangyou when he was taken.

sentences.zh: 又，趙鼎臣《竹隱畸士集》云：當城中之危也，彥卿方與諸將立城上，因泣諫以周、唐強弱，勢不足以相支，又城危甚，而外無一人援，恐旦夕徒死無益，勸彥卿趣降。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhao Dingchen's Collection of the Bamboo Hermit Eccentric states: When the city was in peril, Yanqing was just standing on the wall with the generals; someone wept and remonstrated on the relative strength of Zhou and Tang, saying their force was insufficient to hold out, that the city was in extreme danger and no one outside would aid them, fearing that before long they would die in vain, and urged Yanqing to hurry and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dingchen's Collection of the Bamboo Hermit Eccentric adds that when the city was desperate, Yanqing stood on the wall with his generals. One of them wept and urged surrender, arguing that Zhou and Tang were too unequal in strength to resist, the city was doomed, no relief would come, and they would die for nothing if they held out.

sentences.zh: 彥卿頷之，因顧諸將指曰：「視彼！

translations.literal: Yanqing nodded, then turned to the generals and pointed, saying, "Look there!
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing nodded, then turned to the generals and pointed. "Look there!

sentences.zh: 」諸將方回顧，彥卿則抽劍斷其子首，擲諸地，慷慨泣謂諸將曰：「此彥卿子，勸彥卿降周，彥卿受李家厚恩，誼不降，此城吾死所也。

translations.literal: " As the generals were just turning to look, Yanqing drew his sword and severed his son's head, cast it to the ground, and with passionate tears told the generals, "This is Yanqing's son, who urged Yanqing to surrender to Zhou. Yanqing received great favor from the Li family and by right will not surrender; this city is where I shall die.
translations.idiomatic: " As the generals turned to look, Yanqing drew his sword and cut off his son's head, threw it to the ground, and weeping told them, "This was my son, who urged me to surrender to Zhou. I owe the Li family a deep debt of gratitude and will not yield. This city is where I die.

sentences.zh: 諸軍欲降任降，第勿勸我，勸我者同此子矣。

translations.literal: If any in the army wish to surrender, let them surrender as they please; only do not urge me—whoever urges me will share this son's fate.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you wish to surrender, do so—but do not urge me. Whoever urges me will share my son's fate.

sentences.zh: 」於是諸將愕眙亦泣，莫敢言降。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon the generals stared in shock and wept as well; none dared speak of surrender.)]
translations.idiomatic: " The generals stared in shock and wept; none dared mention surrender again.)]

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅，偽命天長軍使易赟以城歸順。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, the false-appointed Tianchang army commissioner Yi Yun surrendered the city in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, the rebel-appointed Tianchang army commissioner Yi Yun surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 戊午，車駕發楚州南巡。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the imperial carriage departed Chuzhou on a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the imperial procession left Chuzhou on a southern tour.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，駐蹕於廣陵，詔發揚州部內丁夫萬餘人城揚州。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the court halted at Guangling and ordered more than ten thousand corvée laborers from within Yangzhou's jurisdiction to fortify Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the court halted at Guangling and ordered more than ten thousand laborers from Yangzhou's jurisdiction to rebuild the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 帝以揚州焚蕩之後，居民南渡，遂於故城內就東南別築新壘。

translations.literal: Because after Yangzhou was burned and laid waste its inhabitants had crossed south over the river, the Emperor therefore within the old city separately built a new fortification toward the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yangzhou had been burned and its people had fled south across the river, the Emperor built a new fortified quarter in the southeast of the old city.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，遣使祭故淮南節度使楊行密、故升府節度使徐溫等墓。

translations.literal: On wuchen, envoys were sent to sacrifice at the tombs of the former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi and the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen and others.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen envoys were sent to offer sacrifices at the tombs of the former Huainan governor Yang Xingmi, the former Shengfu governor Xu Wen, and others.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，幸揚子渡觀大江。

translations.literal: On guiyou, he visited Yangzi Ford to view the great river.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he visited Yangzi Ford to view the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，黃州刺史司超奏，破淮賊三千人，擒偽舒州刺史施仁望。

translations.literal: On yihai, Huangzhou Prefect Si Chao memorialized that he had broken three thousand Huai bandits and captured the false Shuzhou prefect Shi Renwang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Huangzhou prefect Si Chao reported defeating three thousand Huai rebels and capturing the rebel Shuzhou prefect Shi Renwang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，隰州奏，河東賊軍逃遁。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Xizhou memorialized that the Hedong rebel army had fled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Xizhou reported that the Hedong rebel army had fled.

sentences.zh: 時劉鈞聞帝南征，發兵圍隰州，巡檢使李謙溥以州兵拒之而退。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jun, hearing that the Emperor was campaigning south, raised troops to besiege Xizhou; the inspector Li Qianpu with the prefectural army resisted them and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Northern Han, hearing that the Emperor had marched south, sent troops to besiege Xizhou; inspector Li Qianpu held them off with the prefectural garrison until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》：隰州闕守，乃請監軍李謙溥至隰，並人來圍其城，或請速救之，廷璋曰：「賊遽至，未必攻城。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Yang Tingzhang in the Eastern Capital Epitome: Xizhou lacked a prefect and he therefore requested the military supervisor Li Qianpu to come to Xi; the Bing people came to besiege the city; some urged a rapid rescue; Tingzhang said, "The bandits have come in haste and may not necessarily attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Yang Tingzhang in the Eastern Capital Epitome: With Xizhou lacking a prefect, he asked military supervisor Li Qianpu to take charge at Xi. When the Bing troops came to besiege the city, some urged immediate relief. Tingzhang said, "The enemy came in haste and may not yet assault the walls.

sentences.zh: 」乃募死士百餘人，潛諭謙溥相應，夜銜枚擊之，並人大潰，逐北數十里。

translations.literal: " He then recruited more than a hundred death-defying warriors, secretly instructed Qianpu to coordinate, and at night with gags in their mouths struck them; the Bing people were utterly routed and pursued north for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: " He recruited more than a hundred volunteers, secretly coordinated with Qianpu, and at night led a silent attack. The Bing troops broke completely and were pursued north for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 又，《李謙溥傳》云：隰州闕守，謙溥攝州事，至則浚城隍，嚴兵備。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Biography of Li Qianpu states: Xizhou lacked a prefect; Qianpu took charge of prefectural affairs; upon arrival he dredged the moat and walls and made military preparations strict.
translations.idiomatic: The Biography of Li Qianpu adds that with no prefect at Xizhou, Qianpu took charge, dredged the moat and walls, and tightened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 未旬日而並人至，方盛暑，謙溥服絺绤，揮羽扇，引二小吏登城徐步，並人望之，勒兵不敢動。）〉

translations.literal: Within less than ten days the Bing people arrived; it was the height of summer; Qianpu wore fine hemp and silk, waved a feather fan, and led two junior clerks up onto the wall at an easy pace; the Bing people looked at them and held their troops in check, not daring to move.)]
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the Bing troops arrived. In the height of summer Qianpu wore light hemp, waved a feather fan, and strolled the wall with two junior clerks. The enemy looked on and held their troops back, not daring to move.)]

sentences.zh: 三月壬午朔，幸泰州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renwu the first day of the month, he visited Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day (renwu), he visited Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，復幸廣陵。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he again visited Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he returned to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，幸迎鑾江口。

translations.literal: On xinmao, he visited the river mouth at Yingluan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he visited the Yingluan river mouth.

sentences.zh: 遣右武衛大將軍李繼勛率舟師至江島以觀寇。

translations.literal: He sent Li Jixun, Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guard, to lead the fleet to the river isles to observe the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Jixun, grand general of the Right Wuwei Guard, with the fleet to the river islands to scout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝臨江望見賊船數十艘，命今上帥戰棹以追之，賊軍退去，今上直抵南岸，焚其營柵而回。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Emperor stood by the river and saw several tens of enemy ships; he ordered the Present Emperor to command the war vessels in pursuit; the rebel army withdrew; the Present Emperor went straight to the south bank, burned their camps and palisades, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Emperor looked across the river and saw several dozen enemy ships. He ordered the Present Emperor to lead the warships in pursuit. When the rebels withdrew, the Present Emperor pressed straight to the south bank, burned their camps and stockades, and returned.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以右武衛大將軍李繼勛為左領軍上將軍。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Li Jixun, Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guard, was made Senior General of the Left Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Li Jixun, grand general of the Right Wuwei Guard, was appointed senior general of the Left Leading Army.

sentences.zh: 乙未，殿前都虞候慕容延釗奏，大破賊軍於東氵布州。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Murong Yanzhao, Chief Assistant of the Palace Front, memorialized that he had inflicted a great defeat on the rebel army at East Shuibu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Murong Yanzhao, chief assistant of the Palace Front, reported a major victory over the rebel fleet at East Shuibu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丙申，江南李景遣其臣兵部侍郎陳覺奉表陳情，兼貢羅縠紬絹三千匹，乳茶三千斤，及香藥犀象等。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his minister, Vice Minister of War Chen Jue, to present a memorial stating his case, together with tribute of three thousand bolts of gauze, crepe, and silk, three thousand jin of milk tea, and aromatics, medicines, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Li Jing of Jiangnan sent Vice Minister of War Chen Jue with a memorial pleading his case, together with three thousand bolts of silk and gauze, three thousand jin of milk tea, and aromatics, medicines, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and the like.

sentences.zh: 覺至行在，睹樓船戰棹已泊於江岸，以為自天而降，愕然大駭。

translations.literal: When Jue reached the traveling court and saw tower ships and war vessels already moored on the riverbank, he thought they had descended from heaven and was greatly startled in shock.
translations.idiomatic: When Jue reached the imperial camp and saw tower ships and warships already moored along the bank, he thought they had dropped from the sky and was utterly stunned.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，荊南高保融奏，本道舟師已至鄂州。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Gao Baorong of Jingnan memorialized that his circuit's fleet had already reached Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Gao Baorong of Jingnan reported that his circuit's fleet had reached Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，兩浙錢俶奏，差發戰棹四百艘，水軍萬七千人，已泊江岸，請師期。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Qian Chu of the Two Zhes memorialized that he had dispatched four hundred war vessels and seventeen thousand naval troops, already moored on the riverbank, and requested the date for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Qian Chu of the Two Zhes reported dispatching four hundred warships and seventeen thousand sailors, already moored on the riverbank, and asked for the date to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 己亥，今上率水軍破賊船百餘只於瓜步。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Present Emperor led the navy and broke more than a hundred rebel ships at Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Present Emperor led the navy and destroyed more than a hundred rebel ships at Guabu.

sentences.zh: 是日，李景遣其臣劉承遇奉表以廬、舒、蘄、黃等四州來獻，且請以江為界，帝報曰：「皇帝恭問江南國主。

translations.literal: That same day Li Jing sent his minister Liu Chengyu with a memorial offering Luzhou, Shuzhou, Qizhou, Huangzhou, and the other four prefectures, and also requesting that the river serve as the boundary; the Emperor replied, "The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Jiangnan state lord.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Jing sent Liu Chengyu with a memorial offering Luzhou, Shuzhou, Qizhou, Huangzhou, and three other prefectures, and asking that the Yangtze serve as the border. The Emperor replied, "The Emperor respectfully inquires of the lord of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 使人至，省奏請分割舒、廬、蘄、黃等州，畫江為界者。

translations.literal: Your envoy has arrived; I have reviewed your memorial requesting the partition of Shu, Lu, Qi, Huang, and other prefectures and drawing the river as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoy has arrived, and I have read your request to cede Shu, Lu, Qi, Huang, and the other prefectures and fix the Yangtze as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 頃逢多事，莫通玉帛之歡，適自近年，遂構干戈之役，兩地之交兵未息，蒸民之受弊斯多。

translations.literal: For a time we met with many troubles and could not enjoy the courtesies of silks and gifts; only from recent years did we raise the business of arms; warfare between our two lands has not ceased, and the common people have suffered much harm thereby.
translations.idiomatic: For a time troubles prevented the exchange of gifts and courtesies; only in recent years did war arise between us. Fighting between our two realms has not ceased, and the common people have suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 一昨再辱使人，重尋前意，將敦久要，須盡縷陳。

translations.literal: Yesterday you again honored us with envoys, renewing your former intent, wishing to strengthen a long-standing covenant—I must set it forth in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday you again sent envoys, renewing your earlier intent and wishing to renew our long-standing ties; I must state my response in full.

sentences.zh: 今者承遇爰來，封函復至，請割州郡，仍定封疆，猥形信誓之辭，備認始終之意，既能如是，又復何求。

translations.literal: Now Chengyu has come, your sealed letter has again arrived, requesting the cession of prefectures and districts and still fixing the border—humbly phrased in words of sworn faith, fully acknowledging your intent from beginning to end; since you can act thus, what more is there to seek?
translations.idiomatic: Now Chengyu has come with your sealed letter, asking to cede prefectures and fix the border, with humble words of sworn faith acknowledging your intent from start to finish. Since you offer this, what more could be asked?

sentences.zh: 邊陲頓靜於煙塵，師旅便還於京闕，永言欣慰，深切誠懷。

translations.literal: The frontier will suddenly grow quiet of war dust; the armies will promptly return to the capital—ever speaking of this with joy, with deep and sincere feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier will soon be quiet of war, and the armies will return to the capital. This brings lasting joy and deep sincerity.

sentences.zh: 其常、潤一路及沿江兵棹，今已指揮抽退；

translations.literal: As for the Chang and Run circuit route and the military vessels along the river, orders have now been given to withdraw them;
translations.idiomatic: The forces on the Chang and Run route and the warships along the river have already been ordered to withdraw;

sentences.zh: 兼兩浙、荊南、湖南水陸兵士，各令罷兵；

translations.literal: together with the land and water forces of the Two Zhes, Jingnan, and Hunan—each is ordered to cease arms;
translations.idiomatic: and the land and naval forces of the Two Zhes, Jingnan, and Hunan have each been ordered to stand down;

sentences.zh: 其廬、黃、蘄三路將士，亦遣抽拔近內，候彼中起揭逐處將員及軍都家口丁畢，只請差人勾喚在彼將校，交割州城」云。

translations.literal: the officers and soldiers of the Lu, Huang, and Qi three routes are also being sent to withdraw nearer the interior; when on your side the rolls have been raised and the officers at each post and the household dependents of the army chiefs and corvée laborers are all complete, you need only dispatch men to summon the officers stationed there and hand over the prefectural cities," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: the troops of the Lu, Huang, and Qi routes are also being withdrawn inland. When you have mustered your officers and dependents at each post, send men to summon the commanders still there and hand over the prefectural cities," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，凡得州十四、縣六十、戶二十二萬六千五百七十四。

translations.literal: Huainan was pacified; in all there were gained fourteen prefectures, sixty counties, and 226,574 households.
translations.idiomatic: With Huainan pacified, the Zhou gained fourteen prefectures, sixty counties, and 226,574 households.

sentences.zh: 先是，李景以江南危蹙，謀欲傳位於世子，使附庸於我，故遣陳覺上表陳敘。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Li Jing found Jiangnan in dire peril, he planned to transmit the throne to his heir and make himself a vassal to us; therefore he sent Chen Jue to present a memorial stating his case.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with Jiangnan in peril, Li Jing had planned to abdicate to his heir and become a Zhou vassal, and therefore sent Chen Jue with a memorial stating his case.

sentences.zh: 至是帝以既許其通好，乃降書以答之，曰：「別睹來章，備形縟旨，敘此日傳讓之意，述向來高尚之懷。

translations.literal: At this point, because the Emperor had already agreed to friendly relations with him, he issued a letter in reply, stating, "I have separately seen your incoming document, fully set forth in elaborate wording, narrating your intent to transmit the throne on this day and describing your long-standing lofty sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: Now that friendly relations had been agreed, the Emperor sent a reply stating, "I have read your letter, set forth in full detail, describing your intent to abdicate and your long-standing lofty sentiments.

sentences.zh: 仍以數歲已還。

translations.literal: You also speak of several years already past.
translations.idiomatic: You also speak of the years that have passed.

sentences.zh: 交兵不息，備論追悔之事，無非克責之辭，雖古人有引咎責躬，因災致懼，亦無以過此也。

translations.literal: Warfare between us has not ceased; you fully discuss matters of repentance and regret, all of them words of self-reproach—though the ancients took blame upon themselves and feared calamity, none could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: You speak at length of the war between us and of your repentance, in nothing but words of self-reproach. Though the ancients took blame upon themselves and feared calamity, none went further than this.

sentences.zh: 況君血氣方剛，春秋甚富，為一方之英主，得百姓之歡心。

translations.literal: Moreover, my lord, your vital force is just in its prime and your years are still very full; you are an outstanding ruler of one region and have won the hearts of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you are still in the prime of life, an outstanding ruler of your realm who enjoys the people's devotion.

sentences.zh: 即今南北才通，疆埸甫定，是玉帛交馳之始，乃干戈載戢之初，豈可高謝君臨，輕辭世務，與其慕希夷之道，曷若行康濟之心。

translations.literal: Just now north and south have only just opened relations and the border has only just been fixed—this is the beginning of the exchange of silks and gifts, the first moment when arms are laid aside; how can you loftily decline to rule and lightly abandon worldly affairs? Rather than admiring the way of serene withdrawal, how much better to carry out a heart bent on bringing peace and relief!
translations.idiomatic: North and south have only just reopened relations and the border is only now fixed. This is the beginning of peaceful exchange, the first moment when arms are laid aside. How can you loftily refuse to rule and lightly abandon your duties? Rather than yearning for reclusion, how much better to devote yourself to bringing peace and relief!

sentences.zh: 重念天災流行，分野常事，前代賢哲所不能逃。

translations.literal: I think again that heavenly disasters spread abroad are the common lot of each astral domain—what former ages' wise and worthy could escape?
translations.idiomatic: Remember too that natural disasters are the common lot of every realm—no sage of former ages could escape them.

sentences.zh: 茍盛德之日新，則景福之彌遠，勉修政理，勿倦經綸，保高義於初終，垂遠圖於家國，流芳貽慶，不亦美乎！

translations.literal: If your great virtue renews itself day by day, then your bright blessings will extend ever further—strive to cultivate governance and do not weary of statecraft; preserve your lofty integrity from first to last and leave a far-reaching design for state and family; to leave a fragrant name and bestow blessings—is this not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: If your virtue renews itself daily, your blessings will extend ever further. Strive in governance and do not weary of statecraft. Preserve your integrity from first to last and leave a far-reaching design for your state and house. To leave a fragrant name and bestow blessings—is that not beautiful!

sentences.zh: 」庚子，詔曰：「比者以近年貢舉，頗事因循，頻詔有司精加試練，所冀去留無濫，優劣昭然。

translations.literal: " On gengzi, an edict stated: "Recently, because in these years the tribute examinations have been rather slack and perfunctory, we have repeatedly ordered the responsible offices to test and refine with care, hoping that retention and dismissal would not be lax and that excellence and inferiority would be clear.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengzi an edict declared, "Because recent civil examinations have grown slack, we have repeatedly ordered the responsible offices to test candidates carefully, so that the worthy and unworthy may be clearly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 昨據貢院奏，今年新及第進士等，所試文字或有否臧，爰命辭臣再令考覆，庶涇、渭之不雜，免玉石之相參。

translations.literal: Yesterday, according to the Examination Bureau's memorial, this year's newly passed jinshi and others—the writings they were tested on had some that were faulty or excellent; therefore literary officials were ordered to examine them again, so that Jing and Wei might not be mixed and jade and stone not confused together.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Examination Bureau reported that among this year's newly passed jinshi, some examination essays were faulty. Literary officials were therefore ordered to re-examine them, so that the worthy and unworthy might not be confused.

sentences.zh: 其劉坦、戰貽慶、李頌、徐緯、張覲等詩賦稍優，宜放及第；

translations.literal: As for Liu Tan, Zhan Yiqing, Li Song, Xu Wei, Zhang Jing, and others—their poetry and fu were somewhat superior and they should be allowed to pass;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan, Zhan Yiqing, Li Song, Xu Wei, Zhang Jing, and others wrote somewhat superior poetry and fu and should be allowed to pass;

sentences.zh: 王汾據其文辭，亦未精當，念以頃曾剝落，特與成名；

translations.literal: Wang Fen, judging by his literary compositions, was also not quite refined and apt, but considering that he had recently been stripped of rank, he is specially granted the degree;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen's essays were also not quite adequate, but because he had recently been stripped of rank, he is specially granted the degree;

sentences.zh: 熊若谷、陳保衡皆是遠人，深可嗟念，亦放及第；

translations.literal: Xiong Ruogu and Chen Baoheng are both men from distant regions, deeply worthy of sympathy, and are also allowed to pass;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ruogu and Chen Baoheng are both from distant regions and deeply deserving of sympathy; they too are allowed to pass;

sentences.zh: 郭峻、趙保雍、楊丹、安元度、張昉、董咸則、杜思道等未甚苦辛，並從退黜，更宜修進，以俟將來。

translations.literal: Guo Jun, Zhao Baoyong, Yang Dan, An Yuandu, Zhang Fang, Dong Xianze, Du Sidao, and others did not labor very hard and are all dismissed and rejected; they should further cultivate themselves and await the future.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun, Zhao Baoyong, Yang Dan, An Yuandu, Zhang Fang, Dong Xianze, Du Sidao, and others did not exert themselves sufficiently and are all failed; they should study further and await a future examination.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉、右諫議大夫劉濤選士不當，有失用心，責授右贊善大夫，俾令省過，以戒當官。

translations.literal: Liu Tao, who supervised the examinations and was Right Remonstrance Grandee, selected scholars improperly and failed in his diligence; he was demoted to Right Palatine Grandee and made to reflect on his faults, as a warning to those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, who supervised the examinations as Right Remonstrance Grandee, selected candidates improperly and failed in his duty. He was demoted to Right Palatine Grandee and ordered to reflect on his faults, as a warning to officials.

sentences.zh: 」先是，濤於東京放榜後，引新及第進士劉坦已下一十五人赴行在，帝命翰林學士李昉覆試，故有是命。

translations.literal: " Earlier, after Tao posted the results in the Eastern Capital, he led the fifteen newly passed jinshi including Liu Tan to the traveling court; the Emperor ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to re-examine them, and therefore there was this edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, after Tao posted the results in the Eastern Capital, he brought the fifteen newly passed jinshi including Liu Tan to the imperial camp. The Emperor ordered Hanlin academician Li Fang to re-examine them, which led to this edict.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，復幸揚州，改廬州軍額為保信軍。

translations.literal: On renyin, he again visited Yangzhou and changed Luzhou's army designation to the Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he returned to Yangzhou and redesignated the Luzhou garrison as the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以右龍武統軍趙贊為廬州節度使，以殿前都虞候慕容延釗為淮南節度使兼殿前副指揮使。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Zhao Zan, Commander of the Right Longwu Army, was made military governor of Luzhou; Murong Yanzhao, Chief Assistant of the Palace Front, was made military governor of Huainan and concurrently Deputy Commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Zhao Zan, commander of the Right Longwu Army, was appointed military governor of Luzhou, and Murong Yanzhao, chief assistant of the Palace Front, was made military governor of Huainan and deputy commander of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 遣鹽城監使申屠諤賫書及御馬一十匹、金銀銜全、散馬四十匹、羊千口，賜江南李景。

translations.literal: Shentu E, commissioner of Yancheng Salt, was sent bearing a letter together with ten imperial horses with complete gold and silver bridles, forty loose horses, and a thousand sheep, as gifts to Li Jing of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shentu E, commissioner of Yancheng Salt, was sent with a letter, ten imperial horses with gold and silver bridles, forty additional horses, and a thousand sheep as gifts to Li Jing of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 諤先為王師所俘，故遣之。

translations.literal: E had earlier been captured by the imperial army; therefore he was sent.
translations.idiomatic: E had earlier been captured by the imperial army and was therefore sent on this mission.

sentences.zh: 丙午，江南李景遣所署宰相馮延巳獻犒軍銀十萬兩、絹十萬匹、錢十萬貫、茶五十萬斤、米麥二十萬石。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his appointed chancellor Feng Yanji to present for the army's refreshment one hundred thousand taels of silver, one hundred thousand bolts of silk, one hundred thousand strings of cash, five hundred thousand jin of tea, and two hundred thousand shi of rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his appointed chancellor Feng Yanji with one hundred thousand taels of silver, one hundred thousand bolts of silk, one hundred thousand strings of cash, five hundred thousand jin of tea, and two hundred thousand shi of grain to refresh the army.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔：「故淮南節度使楊行密、故升府節度使徐溫各給守冢戶，應江南臣僚有先代墳墓在江北者，委所在長吏差人檢校。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict stated: "The former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi and the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen shall each be granted tomb-guard households; as for Jiangnan officials and ministers who have ancestral graves north of the river, the local chief officials are entrusted to dispatch men to inspect them."
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict declared that the former Huainan governor Yang Xingmi and the former Shengfu governor Xu Wen would each be granted tomb-guard households, and that ancestral graves of Jiangnan officials north of the river would be inspected by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，李景遣所署臨汝郡公徐遼進買宴錢二百萬並遣伶官五十人與遼俱來獻壽觴。

translations.literal: " On xinhai, Li Jing sent his appointed Duke of Linru, Xu Liao, to present two million in banquet-purchase cash and also sent fifty entertainers to come with Liao and offer the longevity cup.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinhai Li Jing sent his appointed Duke of Linru, Xu Liao, with two million in cash for a banquet and fifty entertainers to offer the longevity toast.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸丑，宴從臣及江南進奉使馮延巳等於行宮，徐遼代李景捧壽觴以獻，進金酒器、禦衣、犀帶、金銀、錦綺、鞍馬等。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, he feasted his attendants and the Jiangnan tribute envoys including Feng Yanji at the traveling palace; Xu Liao, on Li Jing's behalf, raised the longevity cup and presented it, offering gold wine vessels, imperial robes, rhinoceros belts, gold and silver, brocades and silks, saddles and horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guichou, he feasted his attendants and the Jiangnan envoys including Feng Yanji at the mobile palace. Xu Liao raised the longevity cup on Li Jing's behalf and presented gold wine vessels, imperial robes, rhinoceros belts, gold and silver, brocades, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕發揚州還京。

translations.literal: On yimao, the imperial carriage departed Yangzhou to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the imperial procession left Yangzhou for the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，太常博士、權知宿州軍州事趙礪除名，坐推劾弛慢也。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Zhao Li, Doctor of the Grand Secretariat and provisional administrator of Suzhou's military and civil affairs, was struck from the rolls, on the charge of laxity in conducting investigations.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Zhao Li, Doctor of the Grand Secretariat and acting administrator of Suzhou, was expelled from office for laxity in conducting investigations.

sentences.zh: 先是，翰林醫官馬道元進狀，訴壽州界被賊殺卻男，獲正賊，見在宿州，本州不為勘斷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Daoyuan, a Hanlin medical officer, submitted a petition complaining that on the Shouzhou border bandits had killed and robbed his son; the principal culprit had been captured and was presently in Suzhou, but the prefecture would not conduct an investigation and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ma Daoyuan, a Hanlin medical officer, petitioned that bandits on the Shouzhou border had killed his son. The principal culprit had been captured and held at Suzhou, but the prefecture would not try the case.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遣端明殿學士竇儀乘驛往按之，及獄成，坐族死者二十四人。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and sent Dou Yi, academician of the Duanming Hall, traveling by post relay to investigate; when the case was concluded, twenty-four persons were condemned to death extending to their clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and sent Dou Yi, academician of the Duanming Hall, by post relay to investigate. When the case concluded, twenty-four persons were condemned to clan-extinction.

sentences.zh: 儀奉辭之日，帝旨甚峻，故儀之用刑傷於深刻。

translations.literal: On the day Yi received his commission, the Emperor's intent was very stern; therefore Yi's application of punishment tended toward severity and harshness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi received his commission the Emperor's intent was very stern, and Yi's punishments therefore tended toward severity.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以前延州留後李彥頵為滄州留後。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Li Yanfen, former acting governor of Yanzhou, was made acting governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Li Yanfen, former acting governor of Yanzhou, was appointed acting governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，新太廟成，遷五廟神主入於其室。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the new Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed and the spirit tablets of the five temples were moved into its chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the new Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed and the spirit tablets of the five shrines were moved into it.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至自淮南。

translations.literal: On renshen, he arrived from Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he returned from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，命宣徽北院使昝居潤判開封府事。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Zan Jurun, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was ordered to administer Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Zan Jurun, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was ordered to administer Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，澶州節度使張永德準詔赴北邊，以契丹犯境故也。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zhang Yongde, military governor of Cazhou, obeyed an edict to proceed to the northern frontier because the Khitan had violated the border.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Zhang Yongde, military governor of Cazhou, obeyed an edict to proceed to the northern frontier because the Khitan had raided the border.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，兩浙奏，四月十九日杭州火，廬舍府署延燒殆盡。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Two Zhes memorialized that on the nineteenth day of the fourth month Hangzhou caught fire and dwellings and government offices were burned almost entirely away in the spreading blaze.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Two Zhes reported that on the nineteenth day of the fourth month Hangzhou caught fire and dwellings and government offices were nearly all burned.

sentences.zh: 五月辛巳朔，上御崇元殿受朝，仗衛如式。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinsi the first day of the month, the Emperor took the Hall of Venerating the Primordial to receive court, with guards and insignia according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day (xinsi), the Emperor took the Hall of Venerating the Primordial for court with full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 詔：「侍衛諸軍及諸道將士，各賜等第優給。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The various armies of the Palace Guards and the officers and soldiers of all circuits shall each be granted graded preferential rewards."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that the Palace Guard armies and the troops of every circuit would each receive graded preferential rewards.

sentences.zh: 應行營將士歿於王事者，各與贈官；

translations.literal: As for campaign troops who died in the service of the state, each shall be granted a posthumous office;
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers of the campaign army who died in imperial service would each receive a posthumous office;

sentences.zh: 親的子孫，並量才錄用；

translations.literal: their close kin and descendants shall all be appointed according to their talents;
translations.idiomatic: their close kin and descendants would be appointed according to their abilities;

sentences.zh: 傷夷殘廢者，別賜救接。

translations.literal: those wounded, maimed, or disabled shall separately be granted relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: and the wounded, maimed, or disabled would receive separate relief.

sentences.zh: 淮南諸州及徐、宿、宋、亳、陳、潁、許、蔡等州，所欠去年秋夏稅物，並與除放」云。

translations.literal: For all prefectures of Huainan and the prefectures of Xu, Su, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, Cai, and others, the autumn and summer tax goods owed from last year shall all be remitted and canceled," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Tax arrears from last year's autumn and summer harvests in Huainan and in Xu, Su, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, Cai, and other prefectures would all be remitted," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，命端明殿學士竇儀判河南府兼知西京留守事。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Dou Yi, academician of the Duanming Hall, was ordered to administer Henan prefecture and concurrently manage the Western Capital garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Dou Yi, academician of the Duanming Hall, was ordered to administer Henan and concurrently manage Western Capital garrison affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以襄州節度使安審琦為青州節度使；

translations.literal: On xinmao, An Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou, was made military governor of Qingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao An Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou, was appointed military governor of Qingzhou;

sentences.zh: 以許州節度使韓通為宋州節度使，依前兼侍衛馬步都虞候；

translations.literal: Han Tong, military governor of Xuzhou, was made military governor of Songzhou, continuing as before as Chief Assistant of the Palace Cavalry and Infantry;
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong, military governor of Xuzhou, was made military governor of Songzhou while retaining his post as chief assistant of the palace cavalry and infantry;

sentences.zh: 以宋州節度使向訓為襄州節度使；

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, military governor of Songzhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, military governor of Songzhou, was appointed military governor of Xiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 以今上為忠武軍節度使，依前殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: the Present Emperor was made military governor of the Zhongwu Army, continuing as before as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: the Present Emperor was appointed military governor of the Zhongwu Army while retaining his post as commander-in-chief of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 淮南之役，今上之功居最，及是命之降，雖雲酬勛，止於移鎮而已，賞典太輕，物議不以為允。

translations.literal: In the Huainan campaign the Present Emperor's merit ranked first; when this appointment was issued, though it was said to reward merit, it amounted only to a transfer of commandery— the scale of reward was too light, and public opinion did not regard it as adequate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huainan campaign the Present Emperor's merit had ranked first. When this appointment was issued, though called a reward for merit, it amounted only to a transfer of commandery. The reward was too slight, and public opinion did not consider it adequate.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左武衛上將軍武行德為鄜州節度使，以右神武統軍宋延渥為滑州節度使，

translations.literal: On guisi, Wu Xingde, Senior General of the Left Wuwei Guard, was made military governor of Fuzhou; Song Yanwo, Commander of the Right Shenwu Army, was made military governor of Huazhou,
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Wu Xingde, senior general of the Left Wuwei Guard, was appointed military governor of Fuzhou, and Song Yanwo, commander of the Right Shenwu Army, was made military governor of Huazhou,

sentences.zh: （《小畜集·宋延渥神道碑》云：五月，授義成軍節度使，其制略曰：「長驅下瀨之師，若涉無人之境。

translations.literal: (From the Spirit Way Stele of Song Yanwo in the Minor Livestock Collection: In the fifth month he was appointed military governor of the Yicheng Army; the commission in brief stated, "Your army that drove straight down the rapids was as if passing through a land without men.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Spirit Way Stele of Song Yanwo in the Minor Livestock Collection: In the fifth month he was appointed military governor of the Yicheng Army. The commission read in part, "Your army that drove straight down the rapids passed as through an unpeopled land.

sentences.zh: 除兇戡難，爾既立夫殊庸，礪嶽盟河，予豈忘於豐報。

translations.literal: In eliminating villains and quelling calamity you have already established outstanding merit; you have sworn oaths at Mount Li and the Yellow River—how could I forget a rich reward?
translations.idiomatic: In destroying the enemy and quelling disaster you have won outstanding merit; you have sworn oaths at Mount Li and on the Yellow River—how could I forget a rich reward?

sentences.zh: 南燕舊邦，北闕伊邇。

translations.literal: The old domain of Southern Yan lies near; the northern gate is not far.
translations.idiomatic: The old domain of Southern Yan lies near, and the northern capital is close at hand.

sentences.zh: 河壖作翰，遙臨白馬之津；

translations.literal: Take the river bank as your brush and from afar oversee the ford of White Horse;
translations.idiomatic: Take the river bank as your domain and from afar oversee the ford of White Horse;

translations.literal: command troops below Rang and thereupon garrison the land of the Reclining Dragon.")]
translations.idiomatic: command troops at Rang and there garrison the land of the Reclining Dragon.")]

sentences.zh: 以前同州留後王暉為相州留後。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, former acting governor of Tongzhou, was made acting governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, former acting governor of Tongzhou, was appointed acting governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，立東京羅城諸門名額，東二門曰寅賓、延春，南三門曰朱明、景風、畏景，西二門曰迎秋、肅政，北三門曰元德、長景、愛景。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the name plaques of the gates of the Eastern Capital's outer wall were established: the two eastern gates were called Yinbin and Yanchun; the three southern gates Zhuoming, Jingfeng, and Weijing; the two western gates Yingqiu and Suzheng; the three northern gates Yuande, Changjing, and Aijing.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the gates of the Eastern Capital's outer wall were named: the two eastern gates Yinbin and Yanchun; the three southern gates Zhuoming, Jingfeng, and Weijing; the two western gates Yingqiu and Suzheng; the three northern gates Yuande, Changjing, and Aijing.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，幸懷信驛。

translations.literal: On xinchou, he visited Huaixin Post.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he visited Huaixin Post.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔在朝文資官各再舉堪為幕職令錄一人。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict ordered that each civil official at court again nominate one person fit to serve as a staff secretary or county recorder.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi an edict ordered each civil official at court to nominate one person fit for a staff or county recorder post.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以襄州節度使向訓兼西南面水陸發運招討使。

translations.literal: On wushen, Xiang Xun, military governor of Xiangzhou, was additionally made Southwestern land-and-water transport and punitive envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Xiang Xun, military governor of Xiangzhou, was additionally appointed Southwestern land-and-water transport and punitive envoy.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以太府卿馮延魯充江南國信使，以衛尉少卿鐘謨為副。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Feng Yanlu, Minister of the Treasury, was appointed envoy of credence to Jiangnan, with Zhong Mo, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Princes, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Feng Yanlu, Minister of the Treasury, was appointed credence envoy to Jiangnan, with Zhong Mo, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Princes, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 賜李景禦衣、玉帶、錦綺羅縠帛共十萬匹、金器千兩、銀器萬兩、御馬五匹、金玉鞍轡全、散馬百匹、羊三百口。

translations.literal: Li Jing was granted imperial robes, a jade belt, brocade, silk, gauze, and thin silk totaling one hundred thousand bolts, gold vessels weighing one thousand ounces, silver vessels ten thousand ounces, five imperial horses with complete gold and jade saddles and bridles, one hundred ordinary horses, and three hundred sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing was granted imperial robes, a jade belt, and one hundred thousand bolts of brocade, silk, gauze, and thin silk, plus one thousand ounces of gold vessels, ten thousand ounces of silver vessels, five imperial horses with full gold and jade saddles and bridles, one hundred ordinary horses, and three hundred sheep.

sentences.zh: 賜江南世子李宏冀器幣鞍馬等。

translations.literal: Li Hongji, heir apparent of Jiangnan, was granted ritual vessels, silk, saddles, horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongji, heir apparent of Jiangnan, was granted ritual vessels, silk, saddles, horses, and the like.

sentences.zh: 別賜李景書曰：「皇帝恭問江南國主。

translations.literal: Separately Li Jing was granted a letter reading, "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Lord of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing was also sent a letter reading, "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Lord of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 煮海之利，在彼海濱，屬疆壤之初分，慮供食之有闕。

translations.literal: The profits of boiling sea salt lie on your coast; as our borders have just been newly divided, we fear there may be shortages in provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The profits of boiling sea salt lie on your coast; as our borders have only just been divided, we fear there may be shortages in provisions.

sentences.zh: 江左諸郡素號繁饒，然於川澤之間，舊無斥鹵之地，曾承素旨，常在所懷，願均收積之餘，以助軍旅之用。

translations.literal: The prefectures of the Left of the River have long been renowned as wealthy, yet among their rivers and marshes there were formerly no salt fields; your plain assurance has long been on our mind, and we wish to share the surplus from your harvests to assist our army's needs.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures east of the River have long been renowned as prosperous, yet among their rivers and marshes there were formerly no salt flats. Your plain assurance has long been on our mind, and we wish to share the surplus from your harvests to assist our army.

sentences.zh: 已下三司，逐年支撥供軍食鹽三十萬石。

translations.literal: We have ordered the Three Departments to allocate yearly three hundred thousand shi of salt for army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: We have ordered the Three Departments to allocate three hundred thousand shi of salt for army provisions each year.

sentences.zh: 」又賜李景今年曆日一軸。

translations.literal: "] Li Jing was also granted one scroll of this year's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: "] Li Jing was also granted one scroll of this year's calendar.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午，命中書舍人竇儼參定雅樂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on gengwu, Dou Yan, drafting officer of the Secretariat, was ordered to assist in fixing the court music.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month on gengwu Dou Yan, drafting officer of the Secretariat, was ordered to assist in fixing the court music.

sentences.zh: 辛未，放先俘獲江南兵士四千七百人歸本國。

translations.literal: On xinwei, four thousand seven hundred Jiangnan soldiers previously captured were released to return to their native country.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei four thousand seven hundred Jiangnan soldiers previously captured were released to return home.

sentences.zh: 壬申，有司奏禦膳料，上批曰：「朕之常膳今後減半，餘人依舊。

translations.literal: On renshen, the relevant offices submitted the imperial diet provisions; the Emperor wrote in the margin, "My regular meals from now on shall be reduced by half; others remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the relevant offices submitted the imperial diet provisions; the Emperor wrote in the margin, "My regular meals from now on shall be reduced by half; all others remain as before.

sentences.zh: 」癸酉，禘於太廟。

translations.literal: "] On guiyou, the di sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: "] On guiyou the di sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，兵部尚書張昭等撰《太祖實錄》三十卷成，上之，賜器帛有差。

translations.literal: On yihai, Minister of War Zhang Zhao and others completed the thirty-volume Veritable Records of the Taizu; they submitted it, and were granted ritual vessels and silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, and others completed the thirty-volume Veritable Records of the Taizu; they submitted it and were granted ritual vessels and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以中書舍人張正為工部侍郎，充江北諸州水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Zhang Zheng, drafting officer of the Secretariat, was made Vice Minister of Works and appointed land-and-water transport commissioner for the prefectures north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Zhang Zheng, drafting officer of the Secretariat, was made Vice Minister of Works and appointed land-and-water transport commissioner for the prefectures north of the river.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔諫議大夫宜依舊為正五品上，仍班在給事中之下。

translations.literal: On wuyin, an edict ordered that Adviser-Remonstrator should as before be ranked Upper Fifth Rank, Positive, still taking court position below the Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin an edict ordered that Adviser-Remonstrator should remain Upper Fifth Rank, Positive, and still take court position below the Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸未，以右散騎常侍高防為戶部侍郎，以左驍衛上將軍李洪信為右龍武統軍，以左領軍上將軍李繼勛為右羽林統軍，以工部尚書田敏為太子少保，以刑部侍郎裴巽為尚書左丞，以左武衛上將軍薛懷讓為太子太師，以右羽林大將軍李萼為右千牛衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on guimou, Gao Fang, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalier Companion for Dispatches, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Li Hongxin, Senior General of the Left Xiaowei Guard, was made Commander of the Right Longwu Army; Li Jixun, Senior General of the Left Leading Army, was made Commander of the Right Yulin Army; Tian Min, Minister of Works, was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Pei Xun, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Xue Huairang, Senior General of the Left Wuwei Guard, was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; and Li E, Grand General of the Right Yulin Army, was made Senior General of the Right Palace Bull Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn on guimou Gao Fang, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalier Companion for Dispatches, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Li Hongxin, senior general of the Left Xiaowei Guard, was made commander of the Right Longwu Army; Li Jixun, senior general of the Left Leading Army, was made commander of the Right Yulin Army; Tian Min, Minister of Works, was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Pei Xun, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Xue Huairang, senior general of the Left Wuwei Guard, was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; and Li E, grand general of the Right Yulin Army, was made senior general of the Right Palace Bull Army.

sentences.zh: 自敏已下皆致仕。

translations.literal: From Tian Min downward, all retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: From Tian Min downward, all retired from office.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，中書門下新進冊定《大周刑統》，奉敕班行天下。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Directorate of the Chancellery newly submitted the compiled Criminal Code of Great Zhou; by imperial order it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Directorate of the Chancellery newly submitted the compiled Criminal Code of Great Zhou, and by imperial order it was promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，賜諸道節度使、刺史《均田圖》各一面。

translations.literal: On dinghai, each military governor and prefect of every circuit was granted one copy of the Equal-Fields Chart.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai each military governor and prefect of every circuit was granted one copy of the Equal-Fields Chart.

sentences.zh: 唐同州刺史元稹，在郡日奏均戶民租賦，帝因覽其文集而善之，乃寫其辭為圖，以賜藩郡。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen of Tang, when prefect of Tongzhou, had submitted a memorial on equalizing households and popular taxes and rents; the Emperor, reading his collected works, approved it and wrote out its text as a chart to bestow on the frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen of Tang, while prefect of Tongzhou, had submitted a memorial on equalizing households and popular taxes and rents. The Emperor, reading his collected works, approved it and copied its text into a chart to bestow on the frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時帝將均定天下賦稅，故先以此圖遍賜之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was about to equalize and fix taxes throughout the realm, and so first bestowed this chart widely.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was about to equalize and fix taxes throughout the realm, and so first distributed this chart widely.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》載原詔云：朕以寰宇雖安，蒸民未泰，當乙夜觀書之際，較前賢阜俗之方。

translations.literal: (From the Five Dynasties Essentials, the original edict reads: Although the realm is now at peace, the common people are not yet at ease; during the second watch when I read books, I compare methods by which former worthies enriched customs.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Five Dynasties Essentials, the original edict reads: Although the realm is now at peace, the common people are not yet at ease. During the second watch, when I read books, I compare methods by which former worthies enriched customs.

sentences.zh: 近覽元稹《長慶集》，見在同州時所上《均田表》，較當時之利病，曲盡其情，俾一境之生靈，鹹受其賜，傳於方冊，可得披尋。

translations.literal: Recently reading Yuan Zhen's Changqing Collection, I found the Equal-Fields Memorial he submitted while at Tongzhou; comparing the benefits and harms of that time, it thoroughly expresses the situation, so that all living beings in one territory equally received its blessing, recorded in official registers for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, reading Yuan Zhen's Changqing Collection, I found the Equal-Fields Memorial he submitted while at Tongzhou. Comparing the benefits and harms of that time, it thoroughly expresses the situation, so that all the people of one territory equally received its blessing; recorded in official registers, it may be consulted at will.

sentences.zh: 因令制素成圖，直書其事，庶王公觀覽，觸目驚心，利國便民，無亂條制，背經合道，盡系變通，但要適宜，所冀濟務，繄乃勛舊，共庇黎元。

translations.literal: Therefore I had a plain chart made and wrote out the matter directly, so that princes and officials viewing it would be struck at sight, benefiting the state and the people without chaotic regulations, adhering to the classics yet conforming to the Way—all lies in flexible adaptation; one need only suit circumstances, as we hope to serve practical affairs; together with veteran merit, let us shelter the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I had a plain chart made and wrote out the matter directly, so that princes and officials viewing it would be struck at sight—benefiting the state and the people without chaotic regulations, adhering to the classics yet conforming to the Way, all through flexible adaptation. One need only suit circumstances, as we hope to serve practical affairs; together with you, my veteran merit, let us shelter the common people.
